architectureDecisions: D1 — BB-065 is the sole owner of generic benchmark infrastructure. BB-077 consumes @exharness/benchmark from its package root and BENCHMARK_SUBSTRATE_MANIFEST_V1 from the delivered calibrated substrate. Deep imports into packages/benchmark/src/** and direct use of Harbor implementation internals are unsupported.

D2 — BB-077 owns exactly two experiment-specific arm adapters: DIRECT_CODEACT and CORE_SYNC. DIRECT_CODEACT invokes the existing JavaScript CodeAct strategy through a benchmark-owned minimal orchestration shim; CORE_SYNC invokes the same strategy through createAgentRuntime. Neither adapter owns experiment registration, ledger, evidence, accounting or audit persistence.

D3 — The fixed-factor identity binds model route/version, task digest, starting workspace, instruction/prompt, JavaScript CodeAct strategy configuration, executor, capability/tool surface, evaluator, resource ceilings and substrate manifest. The only allowed varying factor is arm=DIRECT_CODEACT|CORE_SYNC.

D4 — Keep the existing development/held-out split: six Terminal-Bench 2.1 development tasks for BB-077 and the four reserved tasks for BB-081. Task digests and environment identities are sealed in the BB-077 cohort manifest; BB-077 hard-rejects held-out task execution.

D5 — Task-specific oracle/nop admissibility may run through the delivered substrate port before the cohort starts, but BB-077 cannot reimplement Harbor reset/artifact/verifier/failure normalization or rewrite the BB-065 generic calibration result. A changed substrate manifest starts a new cohort.

D6 — Preserve the frozen first live model route from the prior research: OpenRouter anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6, provider Anthropic, fallback disabled. Provider-observed charged cost remains primary when present; the frozen 2026-09-27 normalization table remains experiment metadata rather than benchmark-kernel policy.

D7 — Every arm execution is registered through createExperimentRegistration/createBenchmarkUnit and starts/settles through AttemptLedger. Arm adapters return raw producer observations; the shared kernel/substrate owns evidence binding, orthogonal outcome normalization, nullable accounting and audit.

D8 — Economics-specific observations owned by BB-077 are model-turn count, capability/tool-call count, monotonic MODEL/CALL intervals, stable-prefix/dynamic-suffix hashes/bytes and comparison labels. Provider cache/token/cost observations remain nullable kernel accounting inputs; repeated prefix proves ELIGIBLE, not a provider cache hit.

D9 — Run three paired repeats per development task with order DIRECT→CORE, CORE→DIRECT, DIRECT→CORE. Reduce all attempts, including retries and non-accepted outcomes, into paired distributions and medians. No best-of-k filtering, significance claim from the small cohort or opaque overall harness score.

D10 — Freeze the BB-081 handoff before future async results: held-out manifest plus the existing quality/safety/economics/context/interaction/latency gate. BB-077 does not execute async candidate arms and does not publish PROMOTE_ASYNC/KEEP_SYNC; BB-081 owns that decision.

D11 — Dependency enforcement is fail-closed: Worker preflight requires BB-065 DONE, the @exharness/benchmark public exports expected by this plan, and a compatible BENCHMARK_SUBSTRATE_MANIFEST_V1. Missing or incompatible upstream artifacts stop execution rather than triggering a local fallback implementation.
implementationSlices: S0 — Upstream contract preflight: assert BB-065 is DONE; load @exharness/benchmark only from the package root; validate required public exports and BENCHMARK_SUBSTRATE_MANIFEST_V1 compatibility; fail closed with no local fallback.

S1 — Arm adapters: implement DIRECT_CODEACT and CORE_SYNC only. Both use the same JavaScript CodeAct strategy/executor/model/capability contracts; deterministic tests prove all fixed factors match and only orchestration differs.

S2 — Fixed-factor/cohort protocol: materialize development and held-out manifests, pair identity, three-repeat alternating order, task-specific admissibility and hard held-out rejection; bind every unit to the upstream substrate manifest.

S3 — Kernel integration: register experiments/units and route every attempt through AttemptLedger plus upstream evidence/accounting/audit APIs; adapters contribute experiment-specific raw observations only; add negatives for deep imports, direct ledger/evidence writes and local Harbor invocation.

S4 — Economics reducer: derive comparison-specific MODEL/CALL timing, turn/tool counts, cache eligibility labels, accepted quality and known provider cost/token metrics from shared attempt records; preserve UNKNOWN/null and all attempts in denominators.
S5 — Live synchronous baseline: execute the preregistered paired cohort only after S0-S4 pass; emit immutable per-pair records and a multidimensional report without a best-of-k or winner score.

S6 — BB-081 handoff + Living truth: publish comparison/handoff/held-out/gate manifests for BB-081 and update Core-harness Living Docs with measured synchronous baseline capability and limitations; do not execute async candidates.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: BB-077 consumes @exharness/benchmark only through the package root plus the BB-065 substrate manifest/port and does not reimplement generic experiment, AttemptLedger, evidence, accounting, audit or Harbor substrate behavior.

DIRECT_CODEACT and CORE_SYNC share exact model/task/prompt/workspace/tool/evaluator/budget identities and differ only in benchmark-owned direct orchestration versus createAgentRuntime synchronous Core orchestration.

The external development cohort, three paired repeats, alternating arm order and BB-081 held-out set are preregistered; held-out execution is rejected and task-specific admissibility uses the delivered substrate without mutating its generic calibration semantics.

Comparison metrics are derived only from shared benchmark attempt/evidence/accounting records and report a multidimensional vector for quality, known cost/tokens, model turns, tool calls, elapsed time, cache observations, no-progress/failure fingerprints and repeat consistency without an opaque winner score.

Every registered attempt and retry remains in the shared AttemptLedger and comparison denominators; BB-077 never overwrites failed attempts, zero-fills missing usage or derives quality from producer/provider termination.

BB-077 emits a versioned comparison manifest/report contract, held-out manifest and preregistered future gate that BB-081 can consume on the same benchmark backbone without changing BB-065 kernel semantics.
BB-077 changes benchmark comparison tooling and Living truth only; it does not modify packages/benchmark, benchmarks/substrate, Core product runtime or async capability implementation.
